# Conformance fixture format (`conformance-v0.4.json`)

One JSON file, shared by the Node.js (`@rudderstack/ai`) and Python (`rudderstack-ai`) SDKs. Each SDK has a driver that runs every scenario and compares the events it emits with `expected`. Keys are snake_case; drivers map them to their own option names (camelCase in Node.js).

```json
{
  "fixture_version": 1,
  "spec_version": "0.4.0",
  "description": "...",
  "scenarios": [
    { "name": "...", "description": "...", "config": {}, "replies": {}, "steps": [], "expected": [], "exact_numbers"?: true, "per_call_content"?: true }
  ]
}
```

## Per scenario

Start each scenario from a clean state: a fresh in-memory RudderStack client set as the global client, `capture_content`, `emit_llm_calls`, `emit_task_started` and `tool_breakdown` from `config` (all default `false`), `identity_from_cookies` from `config` (default `true`), `redact` from `config` (default `true`: built-in masking, no hook), `azure_deployment_models` from `config` (`azureDeploymentModels` in Node.js), an empty price table, no Azure deployment mapping, and an empty reply queue on the mock LLM server. Claude session ids are unique per scenario, so the SDKs' in-process session usage map needs no reset.

### `config`

`{ "capture_content"?: boolean | <policy>, "emit_llm_calls"?: boolean, "emit_spans"?: boolean, "emit_task_started"?: boolean, "tool_breakdown"?: boolean, "identity_from_cookies"?: boolean, "redact"?: boolean, "azure_deployment_models"?: { <deployment>: <base model> }, "event_rules"?: { "tools": { <tool name>: <rule> } }, "classifier"?: { "intents"?, "outcomes"?, "classify": { "intent"?, "outcome"?, "intent_summary"? } | "throw", "delay_ms"? }, "server_feedback"?: boolean, "evaluator"?: { "scores": [<score>] } | "throw", "credits"?: { "by_model": { <model>: <credits> } } | "throw" }`, passed to `configure`.

A tool rule is an event name (string) or `{ "event", "properties_args"?, "properties"?, "when"? }`, mapped to a real rule as follows: `properties_args: [keys]` is `properties(args, result) = { key: args[key] for each key }` (a missing key is sent as absent, not null); `properties: "throw"` raises instead; `when: "never"` returns false; `when: "throw"` raises. Without `event_rules` there are no rules.

A `capture_content` policy is an object with snake_case keys (`default`, `answer_text`, `llm_calls`, `spans`, `feedback_text`, `score_explanation`, `intent_summary`, `call_reason`, `error_message`; `spans` is a boolean or `{ default, messages, tool_calls, http }`), mapped to the SDK's own option (camelCase in Node.js). Interaction and task `options` may carry `capture_content` in the same form. How levels resolve is fixed by `capture-policy-v0.1.json`.

`capture-policy-v0.1.json` has its own sections: `resolution` (levels to the resolved flags), `invalid` (objects every level must reject), `invalid_at_call_site` (an invalid object in interaction or task options, `level: "interaction" | "task"`, must throw a type error from the call that opens it, before any event), `custom_properties` and `spans`. Any case may carry `not_applicable: { <sdk>: <reason> }` (`node`, `python`, `go`): that SDK's runner reports the case as not applicable, with the reason, instead of running it; other SDKs must run it. Go marks the invalid-object cases not applicable because its types enforce booleans and unknown keys don't compile.

`classifier` is passed as `configure(classifier={classify, intents, outcomes})` (no client or model: the scenarios classify with a deterministic `classify` function). `classify` as an object means `classify(turn)` returns exactly those fields (`intent_summary` as `intentSummary` in Node.js); `"throw"` means it raises. With `delay_ms`, the function returns its result (or raises) after that many milliseconds (Node.js: a promise; Python: an async function when a loop runs, otherwise it sleeps in the worker). Without `classifier`, classification is off.

`server_feedback` (default `true`) is `configure(serverFeedback)` / `server_feedback`. `evaluator` is an evaluator function that returns exactly the listed scores for every turn (each score's keys snake_case: `evaluation_name`, `score_value`?, `score_label`?, `evaluator`, `sampled`?, `explanation`?; camelCased in Node.js), or raises with `"throw"`. Without `evaluator`, evaluation is off.

`credits` is the credits hook (`configure({ credits })` / `configure(credits=...)` / `Options.Credits`): it returns `by_model[call.model]` for every call it is asked about, and no credits for a model not listed; `"throw"` means it raises. Without `credits`, there is no hook.

### `replies`

Exact provider replies, queued per route and served in order, one per request:

| Route                | Endpoint                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `openai.chat`        | `POST /v1/chat/completions`                                                                                                                 |
| `openai.responses`   | `POST /v1/responses`                                                                                                                        |
| `anthropic.messages` | `POST /v1/messages`                                                                                                                         |
| `google.generate`    | `POST .../models/<model>:generateContent` (Gemini API `/v1beta/models/...`, Vertex AI express mode `/v1beta1/publishers/google/models/...`) |
| `google.stream`      | `POST .../models/<model>:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse`                                                                                     |

Each reply is one of:

- `{ "status"?: number, "headers"?: { <name>: <value> }, "json": any }`: a JSON body (`status` defaults to 200), with those extra response headers (a gateway's `x-litellm-response-cost`, `x-litellm-model-name`).
- `{ "status"?: number, "headers"?: { <name>: <value> }, "sse": [{ "event"?: string, "data": any }] }`: a `text/event-stream` body; each entry becomes `event: <event>\ndata: <data>\n\n`, with `data` JSON-encoded unless it is a string (`"[DONE]"`).
- `{ "hang": true }`: accept the request and never answer (the client times out or aborts).
- `sse` with `"hang_after": true`: send the listed events, then keep the connection open without ending it (the client aborts or times out mid-stream).

Replies are complete and fixed; drivers must not rely on any default mock behaviour. Chat streams always end with a usage chunk (`choices: []`), as the API does when `stream_options.include_usage` is set; the SDKs request it on every host.

### Clients

Provider clients point at the mock (`OPENAI_BASE_URL` = `<mock>/v1`, Anthropic and Google Gen AI base URL = `<mock>`), use any API key, and have **retries disabled** (`maxRetries` / `max_retries` = 0; the Google Gen AI clients do not retry by default). The `google.vertex.*` calls use a Vertex AI client in express mode (`vertexai: true` with an API key and no project), so no Google Cloud credentials are needed. LangChain steps use a `ChatOpenAI` on the same mock, or a `ChatAnthropic` with `provider: "anthropic"`.

### `steps`

Run in order. Ops:

| `op`                         | Fields                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Meaning | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `interaction`                | `options`, `steps`, `expect_error`?                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Run `steps` inside `aiInteraction(options)` / `ai_interaction(**options)`. Option keys: `user_id`, `anonymous_id`, `conversation_id`, `feature`, `intent`, `trace_id`, `input_method`, `prompt_text`, `trigger`, `account_id`, `on_behalf_of`, `trigger_source`, `task_name`, `parent_interaction_id`, `tool_breakdown`, `cookies` (a `Cookie` header string or a name-to-value map, passed as is), `identity_from_cookies`, `classify`, `surface`, `trigger_event_id`, `attachment_count`, `attachment_types`, `agent_version`, `variant`, `resume` (the `save_as` name of a paused snapshot, parsed back from its JSON string and passed as the `resume` option; or an inline snapshot object, passed as is, for hand-written snapshots). With `expect_error`, the interaction raises and the driver swallows the error. After the step the driver awaits the SDK's `flush()`, so classifications land before the next step.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `task`                       | `task_name`, `options`, `steps`, `expect_error`?                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Run `steps` inside `aiTask(task_name, options)` / `ai_task(task_name, **options)`. Option keys as for `interaction` minus `trigger`, `task_name` and the prompt keys; `parent_interaction_id` may be `null` (opt out of chaining). Becomes the current interaction, like `interaction`. The driver awaits `flush()` after it, as for `interaction`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `context`                    | `values`, `steps`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Run `steps` inside `aiContext(values)` / `ai_context(**values)`. Keys: `user_id`, `anonymous_id`, `conversation_id`, `feature`, `surface`, `account_id`, `on_behalf_of`, `agent_version`, `variant`, `context`, `cookies`. A top-level `context` step (not nested in an `interaction` or `task`) is followed by the SDK's `flush()`, as for `interaction`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `call`                       | `api`, `params`, `provider`?, `response`?, `stream`?, `request_id`?, `error`?, `stream_error`?, `consume`?, `timeout_ms`?, `abort_after_ms`?, `wrap_twice`?, `call_options`?, `expect_error`?                                                                           | One call through the SDK's wrapped client. `params` is the request body as passed to the client. `api`: `openai.chat` (`chat.completions.create`), `openai.responses` (`responses.create`), `anthropic.messages` (`messages.create`), `anthropic.messages.stream` (the `messages.stream()` helper: iterate it, then read the final message), `google.generate` / `google.stream` (`models.generateContent` / `models.generateContentStream` of a Gemini API client; `params` are their parameters: `model`, `contents`, `config`), `google.vertex.generate` / `google.vertex.stream` (the same on a Vertex AI client), `bedrock.converse`, `bedrock.converse_stream` (see [Bedrock calls](#bedrock-calls)). `provider` (Anthropic and OpenAI APIs): the wrapper is created with that provider label, as for the Bedrock and Vertex Anthropic clients (`wrapAnthropic(client, { provider })` / `wrap_anthropic(client, provider=...)`, e.g. `aws.bedrock`, `gcp.vertex_ai`) or an OpenAI client pointed at a gateway (`wrapOpenAI(client, { provider })` / `wrap_openai(client, provider=...)`, e.g. `openrouter`, `litellm`); the request still goes to the mock. Streams (`params.stream: true`, `bedrock.converse_stream`, and the helper) are iterated to the end, or with `consume: "first_chunk"` the driver stops after the first chunk (`break`). `timeout_ms` sets the client request timeout; `abort_after_ms` aborts the request (AbortSignal / task cancellation) after that delay; an abort mid-stream (`params.stream: true`) may end the stream quietly (the Anthropic Node.js SDK does) or raise (a cancelled Python task): without `expect_error`, drivers swallow an abort or cancellation error raised while consuming such a stream. Other aborts raise as usual. `during: [steps]` (streams only): after the first chunk arrives, the driver runs these steps, then keeps consuming. `call_options` (`{ call_purpose?, fallback_used?, byok? }`): the wrapper is created with those options (`wrapOpenAI(client, { callPurpose, fallbackUsed, byok })` / `wrap_openai(client, call_purpose=..., fallback_used=..., byok=...)`, and the same for the other wrappers). `wrap_twice: true`: the call goes through the SDK's wrapper applied to an already wrapped client (`wrapOpenAI(wrapOpenAI(client))`), as when a library wraps the app's client again. With `expect_error`, the call raises and the driver swallows the error inside the interaction. |
| `raise`                      | `message`, `retry_error`?                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Raise an application error (a plain `Error` / `Exception`) inside the current interaction. With `retry_error: { status }`, raise instead the retry wrapper a retry library throws when it gives up, its last attempt an error with that HTTP status (`status` / `status_code`), not chained to it: Node.js the AI SDK's `RetryError` (`lastError`), Python tenacity's `RetryError` (`last_attempt`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `set_intent` / `set_outcome` / `set_confidence` | `value` | `end`                        | `response_text`?, `extra_properties`?, `status`?, `error_type`?, `pause_reason`?, `block_reason`?, `client_disconnected`? response text, extra (custom) properties, status (passed as is, also when it is not a valid status), error type, pause reason, block reason and `client_disconnected` (`clientDisconnected` in Node.js). | `pause` | `reason`?, `response_text`?, `extra_properties`?, `save_as`? | `pause({ reason, responseText, extraProperties })` / `pause(reason=..., response_text=..., extra_properties=...)` on the current interaction. With `save_as`, the snapshot it returns is serialised to a JSON string and kept under that name, as a store would keep it; `drop_keys` (SDK-6798) first deletes those top-level keys from the saved snapshot (`["call_sequence"]` checks that a snapshot without it restarts `call_index` at 1). |

| `langchain_late_callbacks` | `model`, `metadata` | Drive one `RudderStackCallbackHandler()` directly: root chain run `root` starts (no parent, run metadata `metadata`); model run `model` (parent `root`, metadata `{ ls_provider: "openai", ls_model_name: model }`) starts and ends with one generation whose `AIMessage` carries `usage_metadata` `{ input_tokens: 10, output_tokens: 2, total_tokens: 12 }`; `root` ends. Then, late: model run `late-model` (parent `root`, usage 5 / 1), chain run `late-chain` (parent `root`) starts, model run `late-grandchild` (parent `late-chain`, usage 5 / 1), `late-chain` ends. |
| `openai_agents_run`          | `agents`, `input`, `api`?, `stream`?, `session_id`?, `tracking`?, `expect_error`?                                                                                                                                                                      | One OpenAI Agents SDK run through the integration (`trackedRun(runner, agent, input, options, tracking)` / `tracked_run(agent, input, tracking=..., **options)`; with `stream: true`, `trackedRunStreamed` / `tracked_run_streamed`, every event consumed). `agents` lists `{ name, model, tools?, hosted_tools?, handoffs?, agent_tools?, input_guardrail? }`; the first is the starting agent, and `handoffs` / `agent_tools` name agents later in the list. Each agent has instructions `"Conformance fixture agent."` and its `model` as a string, resolved by an `OpenAIProvider` on a client pointed at the mock: Responses API, or Chat Completions with `api: "chat"`. `tools` are function tools without parameters returning `{"tool":"<name>","ok":true}` (JSON); a name starting with `fail_` raises instead, and one starting with `raise_` raises with the SDK's tool error handling off (Node.js `errorFunction: null`, Python `failure_error_function=None`), so the error ends the run. `hosted_tools: ["web_search"]` adds the hosted web search tool. `agent_tools` adds each named agent as a tool (`asTool({ toolName: name })` / `as_tool(name, ...)`). `input_guardrail: "trip"` adds an input guardrail that runs before the model (not in parallel) and trips. `session_id` passes an in-memory session with that ID (`MemorySession` / `SQLiteSession`). `tracking` holds interaction option keys as for `interaction`, plus `provider`. Agents SDK tracing is enabled with no exporter. With `expect_error`, the run raises and the driver swallows the error.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `claude_messages`            | `prompt`, `options`?, `tracking`?, `frames`                                                                                                                                                                                                            | The Claude Agent SDK integration (`trackedQuery(params, tracking)` / `tracked_query(prompt=..., options=..., **tracking)`) over a scripted transport that emits `frames` (raw `stream-json` messages as the `claude` CLI prints them: `system`, `assistant`, `user`, `stream_event`, `result`) instead of starting the CLI. `prompt` is a string, or `null` for streaming input: the prompt is then an async iterable the driver controls, and a frame `{ "type": "prompt", "text": "..." }` means the app's iterable yields one user message with that text at that point (the transport reads it before emitting the next frame); prompt frames are never emitted as messages. `options` are query options: `resume` (a session id), `continue` (`continue_conversation`), `fork_session`. `tracking` holds interaction option keys as for `interaction` plus `usage_baseline` (`{ "modelUsage": {...}, "total_cost_usd": n }`, the CLI's result shape). Every message is consumed. Inside an `interaction` it reports into it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

### Bedrock calls

`bedrock.converse` and `bedrock.converse_stream` run against an in-memory fake Bedrock Runtime client (no mock server), wrapped with `wrapBedrock` / `wrap_bedrock`. The fake answers from the step:

- `params`: the Converse request (`modelId`, `messages`, `toolConfig`, ...), with the same field names in both SDKs. Node.js sends it as `client.send(new ConverseCommand(params))` / `new ConverseStreamCommand(params)` (the fake receives the real command objects); Python calls `client.converse(**params)` / `client.converse_stream(**params)`.
- `response` (`bedrock.converse`): the Converse output body, returned as is.
- `stream` (`bedrock.converse_stream`): the event objects the response's `stream` yields, in order (`messageStart`, `contentBlockStart`, `contentBlockDelta`, `contentBlockStop`, `messageStop`, `metadata`), each as the SDKs yield it (`{ "contentBlockDelta": { "contentBlockIndex": 0, "delta": { "text": "..." } } }`).
- `request_id`: the AWS request ID on the response: Node.js `$metadata.requestId`, Python `ResponseMetadata.RequestId`. Without it the response has none.
- `error`: `{ "code", "status", "message" }`: the call raises instead of answering. Node.js: `new <code>({ message, $metadata: { httpStatusCode: status } })` with the SDK's exception class of that name (`ThrottlingException`, `ValidationException`, ...). Python: `botocore.exceptions.ClientError({"Error": {"Code": code, "Message": message}, "ResponseMetadata": {"HTTPStatusCode": status}}, "Converse")` (`"ConverseStream"` for the stream API).
- `stream_error`: `{ "code", "message" }`: raised while iterating, after the listed `stream` events, as the SDKs raise modeled stream exceptions. Node.js: `new <code>({ message, $metadata: {} })` thrown from the async iterator; Python: `botocore.exceptions.EventStreamError({"Error": {"Code": code, "Message": message}}, "ConverseStream")` raised from the iterator.

## `expected` and normalisation

`expected` lists every track call the scenario must produce, in emission order. Before comparing, normalise each emitted message to:

```json
{ "event": "...", "userId"?: "...", "anonymousId"?: "...", "properties": {}, "context": {} }
```

- Keep only `event`, `userId`, `anonymousId` (omit when unset or null), `properties` and `context`. Drop every other envelope field (`messageId`, `timestamp`, `originalTimestamp`, `sentAt`, `type`, `integrations`, ...).
- `context`: drop `library`; in `context.wrapperLibrary` drop the top-level `name` and `version` (each SDK sends its own) and keep `specVersion` and `integration`; a nested outer `wrapperLibrary` is kept as is.
- IDs minted by the SDK are UUID v4 strings. An `interaction_id` or `parent_interaction_id` that is a UUID v4 becomes `$int1`, `$int2`, ... (one shared map; within an event `interaction_id` is mapped first) and a `conversation_id` that is one becomes `$conv1`, ..., numbered in order of first appearance within the scenario. Other (caller-supplied) IDs are compared literally.
- `call_index` (SDK-6798): unless the scenario sets `"per_call_content": true`, delete `call_index` from every `ai_llm_response_received` before comparing, so scenarios from before it need not list it. Scenarios named `per_call_content_*` set it and list `call_index`, `input_messages`, `input_truncated`, `output_text` and `output_tool_calls` (see [docs/events.md](../../docs/events.md#ai_llm_response_received)).
- `latency_ms`, `time_to_first_token_ms`, `tool_duration_ms` `classifier_duration_ms` and `total_paused_ms`, when present with a number >= 0, become `"<number>"`; so do `duration_ms` and `max_duration_ms` in each `tool_breakdown` entry. Present vs absent still matters. With scenario `exact_call_timing: true`, the LLM event keeps numeric latency and TTFT so synthetic `record_call.timing` durations are compared exactly. Interaction durations are still normalised.

Then compare:

- Objects by key set and values; key order is ignored. A missing or extra key is a difference.
- Arrays by length and position.
- Numbers by value with a relative tolerance of 1e-9 (`0` equals `0.0`); with `"exact_numbers": true` on the scenario, numbers must be exactly equal.
- Everything else strictly.

Each emitted event must also validate against `spec/ai-events-v0.4.schema.json` (the drivers' usual schema check); a declared tool event (a name not starting with `ai_`, carrying `tool_status`) against `$defs/declared_tool_event`.

## Per-call content rules (SDK-6798)

`ai_llm_response_received` content (`input_messages`, `input_truncated`, `output_text`, `output_tool_calls`) is built in this order. Every SDK must reproduce the `per_call_content_*` scenarios and the tracing `per_call_content_*` cases from these rules alone.

1. **Gate.** Only with `emit_llm_calls` and `capture_content` both on (the interaction's own `capture_content` wins) and the interaction not ended or untracked: content is not built, and the `redact` hook not run, otherwise. Only `call_index` is sent without it. Streamed text is buffered only up to the 32,000 code-point cap.
2. **`call_index`.** 1 plus the sum of `call_count` of every call reported earlier in the interaction (default `call_count` 1), across pauses; a pause snapshot carries it as `call_sequence` (written with `emit_llm_calls` when above 0; absent means a restored run restarts at 1). A report merged into an earlier report of the same call (wrapper and span twin) keeps the first report's index, and a twin with a larger `call_count` adds the difference to the counter. A call folded past `limits.max_calls_per_interaction` keeps the index of the first call it stands for and sends no content. A pending call in a pause snapshot carries its own `call_index` (written with `emit_llm_calls`), so it sends it after restoration.
3. **Part shapes.** Modality is `image`, `audio` or `video` from the media type (`image/png`), else `document` (PDFs, text and any other file); the GenAI semconv names no document modality, so this is the SDK convention. Parts: `text`, `reasoning`, `tool_call`, `tool_call_response`, `uri` (`modality`, `uri`, `mime_type`?), `blob` (`modality`, `mime_type`?, never bytes) and `file` (`modality`, `mime_type`?, `file_id`: a file the provider holds by ID, e.g. an OpenAI `file_id` or an Anthropic `source.type: "file"`). Audio formats map to `audio/<format>` (`mp3` is `audio/mpeg`). An Anthropic `text` source is a `text` part, a `content` source maps its blocks. A part kind with no mapping is `{ "type": <provider type name> }`. A tool result's content blocks are mapped with the same rules: text only is one string, otherwise the list of parts; a single Bedrock `json` block is its value.
4. **Binary content sanitization.** With spans on and off, capture uses the app's own serializer (`toJSON` in Node, python-mode `model_dump` in Python, `MarshalJSON` / `MarshalText` with `encoding/json` precedence in Go) before content projection. Raw bytes in its result are stripped; serializer text, including base64, is sent as is under the existing masking and capture controls. A failing serializer becomes JSON `null` without walking its fields. See the serializer-capture fixture below for report lifetime and counter semantics. Before anything else, values are copied to plain JSON: a value that refers back to an object on its own path (a cycle) or sits deeper than 64 levels (counted from the messages or tool-calls list) is left out (its key or array element is dropped), a big integer becomes its decimal string, a date its ISO string, and functions, symbols and undefined are left out; if building a content field still fails, only that field is left out and the call is still sent. After mapping, every message part and tool argument goes through one sanitiser, whatever produced it: (a) a byte array is deleted from its object or array (native byte buffers, an object whose keys are all decimal integers with values 0 to 255, e.g. a JSON-serialised byte array, and `{ "type": "Buffer", "data": [0..255, ...] }`); (b) a string starting with a `data:` URI (`data:[<media type>][;params],`, any case) becomes `data:<media type>` (the payload is cut); (c) an object with a `mime_type`, `mimeType`, `media_type`, `mediaType` or `source_type` key, or whose `type` is `image`, `audio`, `video`, `document`, `file`, `media`, `blob`, `image-data`, `file-data`, `input_audio`, `input_image` or `input_file`, loses its `data`, `bytes`, `base64` and `b64_json` keys. Objects without those markers keep a `data` key. A `uri` part whose `uri` is a `data:` URI becomes a `blob` part (its `mime_type`, else the URI's media type), and a `blob` part loses its `content`.
5. **Per-string cap.** Every string longer than 32,000 code points (`MAX_MASKED_CODE_POINTS`) is cut to its first 32,000 code points, and `input_truncated` is true. This runs before masking.
6. **Masking.** Every string in messages and tool arguments goes through the same masking as `prompt_text` (built-ins, then the `redact` hook). If the hook fails or withholds one string, the whole field is left out (`input_messages` together with `input_truncated`, or `output_tool_calls`); `output_text` is left out on its own.
7. **Tool arguments.** A JSON-string `arguments` is parsed to its JSON value; a string that is not valid JSON (a cut-off stream) stays a string. Calls without a name are skipped.
8. **Event size.** After the SDK's other properties are added (sampling stamp included), the measure is the compact JSON (`JSON.stringify`, no spaces, key order as emitted) of the event `properties`, in UTF-8 bytes, against the 30,000-byte cap. If over, in this order, stopping as soon as it fits:
   1. While `properties` without `input_messages` and `input_truncated` is still over the cap, delete `output_text`, then `output_tool_calls`. If the event now fits, stop (`input_truncated` unchanged).
   2. Set `input_truncated` to true. `over` is bytes over the cap.
   3. Drop messages: starting right after the leading run of `system` messages, delete the oldest message, subtract its compact JSON bytes + 1 (the comma) from `over`, and repeat while `over` > 0 and more than one message remains after that run. The last message always stays (when every message is `system`, none is dropped).
   4. Shorten: while `over` > 0, pick the string to cut among the string values found under any `content`, `response` or `arguments` key (at any depth) of the remaining messages. Strings of messages with a role other than `system` are chosen first; strings of `system` messages only when no other string has a character left. The longest (in code points) wins; on a tie the first in message order, then in document order. Remove code points from its end one at a time, subtracting each one's UTF-8 bytes inside a compact JSON string (a character JSON escapes counts its escape), until `over` <= 0 or the string is empty. Repeat with the next pick.
   5. If every candidate is empty and `over` is still > 0, delete `input_messages` and `input_truncated`.
   6. If the event is still over, delete `output_text`, `output_tool_calls`, `response_text`, `prompt_text` in that order until it fits, then `action_details.feedback_text`, then `tool_breakdown` and `usage_breakdown` entries from the end.
   An event that fits keeps all content and sets `input_truncated` only from rule 4.

## Rules the expected events encode

- No `spec_version` property: every event carries `context.wrapperLibrary.specVersion: "0.4.0"` on the SDK's own level.
- Minted `interaction_id` and fallback `conversation_id` values are UUID v4; the SDK never invents an `anonymousId` when a `userId` is set (`ai_system` only when there is no identity).
- Every `usage_breakdown` entry has `total_tokens` (input + output).
- `reasoning_tokens` (per call and per `usage_breakdown` entry) and `total_reasoning_tokens` are provider-reported reasoning tokens, a subset of output tokens (never added to them again, never more than them). A reported `0` is sent; a provider or call that reports no count (Bedrock, an Anthropic response without `output_tokens_details`, a failed call) has no field, never an estimate or `0`. Anthropic: `usage.output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens` (Messages API extended thinking; already inside `output_tokens`, the last streamed value wins); Claude Agent SDK: `modelUsage[model].thinkingTokens` (already inside `outputTokens`; a turn delta like the other counters, split over a model's agents in proportion to their output tokens; absent on CLI versions that do not record it, and then no field), and an entry or answer has one when at least one of its calls reports a count (the sum of those).
- Google Gen AI: input = `promptTokenCount` (which includes `cachedContentTokenCount`) + `toolUsePromptTokenCount`; output = `candidatesTokenCount` + `thoughtsTokenCount`, and `thoughtsTokenCount` is also `reasoning_tokens`; so input + output = `totalTokenCount`. `cachedContentTokenCount` is `cached_input_tokens`. Streamed `usageMetadata` is a running total: the last value wins, never a sum. Tool calls come from the `functionCall` parts (Gemini reports `STOP` for them too). `finish_reason` is normalised as for Bedrock: `STOP` is `stop` (`tool_calls` when a part calls a function), `MAX_TOKENS` is `length`, the safety, recitation, blocklist, prohibited-content and SPII reasons are `content_filter`, and so is a blocked prompt (`promptFeedback.blockReason`, a success with no candidates); other values pass through. Provider `gcp.gemini` (Gemini API) or `gcp.vertex_ai` (Vertex AI), the OpenTelemetry `gen_ai.provider.name` values every integration sends, priced separately (see Prices).

- The last model call decides the status: a failed final call gives `response_status: error` (or `timeout` / `cancelled`) and its `error_type`, even after earlier successes; a successful retry is a success. An error raised out of the interaction sets the status from that error.
- The held `ai_user_prompt_created` is sent when the first model call starts: an intent set before that is on it, one set during or after the first call only on `ai_response_received`.
- Empty strings for `user_id`, `anonymous_id`, `conversation_id` and `feature` (interaction and `track_action` options) are absent: the context's value applies.
- `primary_model` / `primary_provider`: the last successful call; when no call succeeded (an error, timeout or cancelled answer), the last attempted call.
- A stream closed before it completed (`break`, abort) is a cancelled call: `error_type: cancelled`, tokens seen so far, no `cost_usd`; the answer is `cancelled` when it was the last call.
- Cost precedence: a cost the provider, gateway or framework reported wins (OpenRouter and the LiteLLM proxy's `usage.cost`, else the LiteLLM proxy's `x-litellm-response-cost` header; a number, or a decimal string such as `"1.5e-05"`; null, blank or negative is no cost), then a registered price, otherwise no cost.
- No cost the SDK does not know: failed and cancelled calls carry no `cost_usd` (unless a framework reported one) and add nothing to totals; a priced `0` is sent. `total_cost_usd` (and an entry's `cost_usd`) is the sum of the priced calls, sent only when at least one call is priced and every successful call is.
- A failed Responses API response keeps its usage; its per-call event has `finish_reason: failed` and `error_type: api_error`.
- `finish_reason` uses Chat Completions' terms on both OpenAI APIs: a completed Responses API output with only tool calls (no message) is `tool_calls`; `incomplete` with `max_output_tokens` is `length` (other reasons as sent, e.g. `content_filter`); a refusal (Chat `message.refusal`, a Responses `refusal` content part) is `refusal`; a streamed Chat refusal keeps the wire's `finish_reason`.
- A completed call is a success whatever its `finish_reason`: a refusal, a content filter, or output cut off at `length` (structured or not) is billed and returned, so it is visible through `finish_reason`, not through `response_status`. Only an exception the app gets fails the answer: the OpenAI parse helpers throwing `LengthFinishReasonError` / `ContentFilterFinishReasonError` give `response_status: error` with `error_type` `length` / `content_filter`, and the call keeps its usage and price.
- A non-streamed Responses API request with `background: true` is only queued: it passes through untracked (no call, and no interaction of its own).
- Streamed chat requests carry `stream_options.include_usage` on every host; a request the host rejects with HTTP 400 or 422 that names the parameter or carries no error code is sent once more as the app wrote it, and only that request is recorded. A coded rejection (a content filter, a prompt too long) is never resent.
- An error is mapped through retry and framework wrappers to the error that caused it (`lastError` / `cause`; Python: tenacity `last_attempt`, `__cause__`, then the implicit `__context__`).
- A call seen by two wrappers (a client wrapped twice) is recorded once: a failed call by the first wrapper that sees the error, and a repeated response adds no tool calls.
- LangChain: a model run's usage is the sum over its prompts (the first generation of each); chunk usage adds up, as LangChain merges chunks; a cancelled or aborted model run keeps the usage streamed so far (unpriced). A retriever run attaches like a chain run: a root retriever run owns its answer. A tool run inside another tool run (a Deep Agents subagent inside `task`) has that enclosing tool as `parent_tool` in `tool_breakdown`, unless run metadata `parent_tool` names one. A Gemini model's (provider `gcp.gemini` / `gcp.vertex_ai`) own finish reasons map as for Google Gen AI (`STOP` `stop`, `MAX_TOKENS` `length`, the safety and other blocked reasons `content_filter`), read from `response_metadata.finish_reason`, else the generation info's `finish_reason` / `finishReason`.
- `tool_call_count` counts every tool the model invoked, including Anthropic `server_tool_use` / `mcp_tool_use` and Responses API `*_call` items.
- Gateways and routers (shared table: `spec/fixtures/providers-v0.1.json`): a call through `openrouter`, `litellm` or `gateway` whose model has a vendor prefix (`openai/gpt-4o`) is reported under that vendor (`openai`), with the full name in `model`. The served model is the response's `model`, or the LiteLLM proxy's `x-litellm-model-name` header when present (its body `model` is the alias the app asked for). `requested_model` is the request's model, sent on `ai_llm_response_received` and `usage_breakdown` entries only when the served model differs from it beyond a vendor prefix or version suffix (`gpt-4o` served as `openai/gpt-4o-2024-08-06` sends none). Bedrock's `[region.]anthropic.` prefix and `-v<n>:<n>` suffix, and Vertex's `@<date>` (read as `-<date>`), are the same model as Anthropic's ID (`us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0` or `claude-haiku-4-5@20251001` served as `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` sends none). A streamed chat completion's final usage chunk may carry one choice with an empty delta that repeats `finish_reason` (OpenRouter): it is the same call's finish, not another one.
- Prices: a registered name prices a model with exactly that name, or that name followed by a version suffix (dates `-YYYY-MM-DD` / `-YYYYMMDD`, `-NNN` / `-NNNN`, `-v<n>[.<n>]`, `:<tag>`, `@<version>`, `-latest`, in any sequence), never another model of the family (`gpt-4o` does not price `gpt-4o-mini`). A model with a vendor prefix also matches by the name after its last `/` (`openai/gpt-4o-2024-08-06` as `gpt-4o`; the full name wins a tie). A provider-specific price matches only its provider and the labels naming the same service: `gcp.gemini` and its alias `google` (the Gemini API), `gcp.vertex_ai` and its alias `google.vertex` (Vertex AI), so a price registered under an alias prices the calls; the Gemini API and Vertex AI never share prices. The longest matching name wins, then a price for the call's own provider, then one for a same-service label, then a generic one; `configure(prices)` merges. Costs are rounded half-up to 8 decimals. `cache_write_1h_per_mtok` prices Anthropic 1-hour cache writes (`cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens`), defaulting to `cache_write_per_mtok`.
- Cloud model IDs: for provider `aws.bedrock` the model is matched as sent, then without a leading inference-profile prefix (`us.`, `us-gov.`, `eu.`, `apac.`, `jp.`, `au.`, `in.`, `global.`), then without its vendor prefix (up to the first `.`: `anthropic.`, `amazon.`, ...); the longest registered name wins, then a provider-specific price, then the earlier (more literal) form. No other provider has prefixes stripped. Vertex `claude-...@<revision>` matches through the `@<version>` suffix. For provider `azure.ai.openai` a deployment name in `azure_deployment_models` is priced as its base model; events keep the deployment name; nothing is inferred without a mapping.
- Bedrock Converse: `input_tokens` = `inputTokens + cacheReadInputTokens + cacheWriteInputTokens` (AWS `inputTokens` excludes the cache), `cached_input_tokens` = `cacheReadInputTokens`, cache writes priced at `cache_write_per_mtok`; streams take usage only from the `metadata` event. `finish_reason` from `stopReason`: `end_turn` / `stop_sequence` → `stop`, `tool_use` → `tool_calls`, `max_tokens` → `length`, `guardrail_intervened` / `content_filtered` → `content_filter`, anything else as sent. `response_id` is the AWS request ID, `model` the request `modelId`. A stream that ends without `messageStop` is a failed `api_error` call. A failed stream call (an exception while iterating, or no `messageStop`) keeps the `response_id` and counts the tools seen so far; it ends an interaction the wrapper opened itself, never one the app opened. Error types: a name or code containing `throttling` is `rate_limit`, `accessdenied` `auth_error`, `validationexception` `invalid_request` (case-insensitive), otherwise the HTTP status decides as for other providers.
- LangChain outside an interaction: the handler opens a `user`-triggered interaction (prompt event included) with identity from run metadata; `agent_name` from `agent_name` / `lc_agent_name` metadata or an `agent:<name>` tag.
- Claude Agent SDK `modelUsage` rows whose model has no assistant message and ran no subagent (a subagent tool result's `resolvedModel`) in a tracked stream are internal CLI bookkeeping calls: they do not contribute to `llm_call_count`, tokens, cost or `usage_breakdown`. The primary model's row is always kept. A turn with a subagent whose model is unknown, and standalone result mapping (no message stream), keep every reported row.
- Background fields (`account_id`, `on_behalf_of`, `trigger_source`, `task_name`, `parent_interaction_id`) are on every event of an interaction when set (`ai_user_action`: `account_id`, `on_behalf_of`), never null or empty, and SDK-owned: extra properties with those names are ignored. `account_id` / `on_behalf_of` fall back to the context.
- `aiTask`: `trigger: system`, no prompt event, never the enclosing `userId` / `anonymousId`. Without `parent_interaction_id` it chains to the current interaction (and takes its `conversation_id`); an explicit one wins (no conversation inherited); `null` opts out. `trigger_source` defaults to `agent` whenever there is a parent. Otherwise `conversation_id` is minted (the context's is not used).
- Pauses (Since v0.4): `end(status: paused)` is equivalent to `pause()`. `pause()` sends `ai_response_received` with `response_status: paused`, `pause_reason` (default `other`) and the totals of the calls since the start or the last resume only; the next segment starts from zero. A model or tool call recorded while paused resumes the interaction. Pausing a paused interaction, or one that ended, sends nothing. `aiInteraction` / `aiTask` leave an interaction paused when their body returns (an error still ends it); `end()` while paused ends it. The final answer of an interaction that paused adds `pause_count` and `total_paused_ms`; paused answers have neither. A `resume` snapshot continues the same interaction: its IDs, identity and background fields win over the options, and no prompt event or `ai_task_started` is sent. Response-ID deduplication survives pauses and JSON restoration: snapshots retain bounded `seen_response_ids` provider/ID pairs. Pause flushes adapter finalization before producing its snapshot, marks itself paused before callbacks emit events, and ignores reentrant ends during that transition. Normal bound-stream completion and stale TTL/shutdown selections leave a paused interaction resumable. Reentrant pauses never wait on their own callbacks. Writes accepted after segment capture remain pending for the next segment; snapshots carry `pending_calls` and `pending_tools` across JSON restoration without replaying call events (see `pause-pending-usage-v0.1.json`).
- `ai_task_started` (`emit_task_started`): one per `aiTask` run, sent when it starts with the run's IDs and background fields (no `trigger`), tagged `manual` before any call; never on a resume.
- `tool_breakdown` (opt-in) is one entry per agent/MCP server/tool/parent combination, built from the same de-duplicated calls as `tool_call_count`, so the `call_count`s sum to it. Flat `mcp__server__tool` names split into `mcp_server` and `tool_name`; unnamed calls are `unknown`.
- `error_count` counts known failures. `error_types` uses only `rate_limit`, `timeout`, `cancelled`, `denied`, `auth_error`, `invalid_request`, `connection_error` and `api_error`; unknown categories become `api_error`, never raw messages.
- `duration_ms` sums measured durations even with partial coverage; `measured_count` is that coverage and `max_duration_ms` the maximum. Nested durations with `parent_tool` are inclusive.
- Entries sort by `agent_name`, `mcp_server`, `tool_name`, `parent_tool` (absent sorts as empty), in UTF-16 code-unit order. An explicit `mcp_server` wins over the one in an `mcp__server__tool` name; `error_type` only categorises a call that failed (`error: true`). A tool span without a provider ID completes an earlier call of the same tool and MCP server whose agent and parent tool match or are unknown on either side.
- Claude Agent SDK attribution: a subagent's messages (`parent_tool_use_id` set) take the `subagent_type` input of the `Task` / `Agent` call that launched them (else the message's own `subagent_type`, which the Python SDK does not expose); main-loop messages have no `agent_name`. Their tools carry that `agent_name` and `parent_tool`, the launching call's tool name when it was seen. A finished subagent's last call (its answer) is not streamed: when the launching call's tool result (`tool_use_result`) carries `usage`, that call counts as one more call of the subagent on its `resolvedModel` (unless its input side equals the subagent's last streamed message, the same call). Each model's turn totals are split over its (agent, loop) groups: as observed when they add up; else the main loop keeps `result.usage` (exact) and the other groups share the rest, when none of it goes negative; else each token kind in proportion to what was observed (largest remainders); the model's cost is split by Claude price ratios (input 1, cache read 0.1, cache write 1.25, output 5), the last group (the main loop when present) taking the rest, so entries always add up to `modelUsage`. A query that neither resumes nor continues a session never treats its first result as cumulative.
- OpenAI Agents SDK: one run is one interaction (it joins an active one). Every model response is one call attributed to the agent that made it (`agent_name`), with the agent's configured model name; a nested run of an agent used as a tool reports the model name from its trace span. `finish_reason` is `stop` for a completed response; a response cut off at the output-token limit (Responses `status: incomplete` with `incomplete_details.reason: max_output_tokens`, Chat Completions `finish_reason: length`) is `length`, never the raw `incomplete` status, and keeps its usage even though the Agents SDK raises on the Responses case; the run is then `response_status: incomplete` with `error_type: length`, as for other providers (Chat `content_filter` is kept as sent). Model-requested tools (function, hosted, handoffs as `transfer_to_<agent>`) are tool calls; a local function tool's execution adds its outcome (the Agents SDK's "An error occurred while running the tool." output is a failure) and duration. A guardrail tripwire is `response_status: error` with `error_type: guardrail_trip`. A provider error fails the call in flight and the run; calls before it keep their usage. The session ID is the `conversation_id` unless one is given.
- Bedrock: a call's tool outcome comes from the `toolResult` block a later request in the same interaction sends back (`status: "error"` is a failure).
- Identity from cookies (RudderStack JavaScript SDK v3): `rl_anonymous_id` → `anonymousId`, `rl_user_id` → `userId` (fallback only: not when any explicit or context `user_id` or `anonymous_id` is set), the `rl_session` object's `id` → `context.sessionId` (a number; `sessionStart` is never sent; none when its numeric `expiresAt` is in the past). Explicit interaction options > `aiContext` values > cookies. Unreadable cookies are skipped. `identity_from_cookies: false` (global, or per interaction, which wins) ignores cookies, also for a `track_action` inside that interaction. `aiTask` never reads cookies.
- Opt-in text (`prompt_text`, `response_text`, `action_details.feedback_text`) is masked by the built-in patterns by default, exactly as `spec/fixtures/redaction-v0.1.json` specifies (`[email]`, `[phone]`, `[card]`, `[ip]`, `[secret]`, `[ssn]`, `[iban]`); text over 32000 code points is withheld (not sent). `redact: false` sends it unmasked.
- `ai_user_action`: `action_details` is omitted when nothing is left in it (for example only a `feedback_text` that capture is off for).
- Declared tool events: one track event per tool call of a tool with a rule, named by the rule, at most once per call (the same de-duplicated calls as `tool_call_count`). It is sent as soon as the call is settled (its outcome, or an output without an outcome, is seen: an Anthropic `tool_result`, an OpenAI `role: tool` message or Responses `*_call_output` item in a later request of the interaction, a LangChain tool end/error), otherwise when the interaction ends, just before `ai_response_received`. Properties: the rule's `properties()` output first, then the interaction's IDs and background fields, `trigger`, `agent_name` (when the call has one), `tool_name`, `tool_call_id` (the provider's ID; absent for calls without one, such as a LangChain tool run without a tool call), `tool_status` (`success` / `error` from the outcome, else `unknown`) and `tool_duration_ms` (measured only, rounded; never `0` with `unknown`). SDK-owned names in `properties()` output are dropped. `when()` false or raising sends nothing; `properties()` raising sends the event without custom properties, and so does `properties()` output that takes the event's properties over the 30,000-byte budget (serialized JSON, UTF-8), which otherwise applies to every event, `mcp_*` included: over it, captured text goes first (`response_text`, `prompt_text`, `action_details.feedback_text`), then `tool_breakdown` and `usage_breakdown` entries from the end. Arguments and results are never sent otherwise.
- Intent classification (`classifier` configured): each interaction that ends with `response_status: success` and has classification on sends one `ai_interaction_classified`. On by default only for interactions the app opens itself (`aiInteraction` / `startInteraction`) with `trigger: user`; off for `aiTask` unless the task option `classify: true`, and off for interactions an integration opens on its own (a call outside any interaction, a LangChain handler run, a Claude query turn) unless that integration is given `classify: true`; the interaction option `classify: false` opts out. It is sent after its `ai_response_received`, never before and never blocking it. Properties: the interaction's IDs and background fields, `trigger`, `intent` (the classifier's value when it is one of `intents`, any non-empty string when no `intents` are configured, else `other`), `outcome` (one of `outcomes`, default `resolved`, `partial`, `unresolved`, `unclear`; else `unclear`), `intent_summary` (from `classify` whenever it returns one; from a model client only with `intent_summary: true`; masked like other text, then whitespace collapsed, cut to the first sentence, at most 25 words and 280 characters (code points), and withheld when it still matches a pattern or masking fails), `classifier` (`custom` for `classify`, `model` for a model client), `classifier_model` (model only), `classifier_duration_ms`, `classifier_cost_usd` (model only, when priced; never added to `total_cost_usd`). A raising or timed-out classifier, or an unparseable reply, sends nothing.

## MCP rules

The fixture steps cannot drive an MCP server, so these rules are written here and each SDK's own MCP tests cover them.

- `call_index` counts the reported `mcp_tool_called` events of a scope (`mcp_session_id`, else a caller-sent `interaction_id`) from 0, with no gaps. On 2026-07-28 a `tools/call` answered with `resultType: "input_required"` sends no `mcp_tool_called`; it takes the scope's next position, and the retry that carries `inputResponses` for one of its elicitations keeps that position (`call_index` and `ms_since_previous_call`) instead of taking a new one, and has no `retry_count`. A call, then an elicited call: `call_index` 0, then 1 (never 2). A retry whose `input_required` leg this process does not know (expired or answered elsewhere) is counted as a new call.
- `argument_keys` (`mcp_tool_called`, `mcp_event_subscription_changed`) and `client_capabilities` are sorted by Unicode code point (UTF-8 byte order; `B`, `a`, `b`, `\uFF5E`, `\u{1F600}`), not the client's order, then capped at 100 names. JavaScript's default `sort` compares UTF-16 code units and puts `\u{1F600}` before `\uFF5E`.
- `mcp_event_delivered`: a delivery without a `subscription_id` or an `event_id` (absent, not a string, or empty after trimming) sends nothing and logs one warning per process; the app's sender still runs and its result or error is returned unchanged. It is never sent with `unknown` for either ID. `mcp_event_subscription_changed` likewise sends nothing without a `subscription_id` or `event_name`.

# Cookie fixture format (`cookies-v3.json`)

Generated by `scripts/generate-cookies-fixture.mjs` with `@rudderstack/analytics-js-cookies`; both SDKs must reproduce it exactly.

- `values[]`: `{ name, description, raw, decoded }`. `raw` is a cookie value as it appears in a `Cookie` header. Decoding: URL-decode it (`decodeURIComponent`; invalid percent-encoding or invalid UTF-8 → unreadable, and `+` stays `+`); an empty result is unreadable; with the `RS_ENC_v3_` prefix, base64-decode the rest (Node's `Buffer` rules: missing padding is fine) to UTF-8; then `JSON.parse`. Any failure gives `null`.
- `identities[]`: `{ name, description, cookies, expected }`. `cookies` is a header string or a name-to-value map. A header splits on `;`; each segment splits on its first `=`, name and value trimmed; segments without `=` or with an empty name are skipped; a repeated name keeps the last value. Map values are decoded the same way. `expected` has `anonymous_id` / `user_id` when the decoded value is a non-empty string, and `session_id` when `rl_session` decodes to an object whose `id` is a positive integer number (a safe integer).

## Additions since v0.4 (SDK-5989)

`one_shot` is an interaction/task option: `oneShot` in Node.js, `one_shot` in Python, `OneShot` in Go. It defaults to false. Without an explicit or context conversation ID, true uses `interaction_id` as the required `conversation_id`; otherwise the SDK still generates a separate conversation ID. Explicit IDs and inherited chat/task conversations keep their existing precedence. The one-shot conformance scenarios test generated and custom IDs, explicit/context precedence, and the unchanged chat default.

The migration fixtures cover client events and fields since v0.4, web/mobile surfaces, actionable suggestions, scoped feedback and declared client tool events, including invalid properties. The server schema and emitted spec version are v0.4; the client schema remains v0.2. The migration checker accepts both 0.3.0 and 0.4.0 captures.

### SDK-5990 review regressions

The `v04_review_*` scenarios cover custom server fields, nested version scopes, provider context-limit errors and null tool results. Newly added server fields from app extra properties survive when the SDK leaves them unset; computed SDK values win when present, including zero credits. An explicit JSON null result is four UTF-8 bytes and settles the tool call; an omitted result stays absent. Go integrations carry observed-result presence through the internal hook bridge. For manual Go reports, `Result: nil` retains its existing absent meaning; `json.RawMessage("null")` represents explicit JSON null.

`context-errors-v0.1.json` fixes provider messages, codes and HTTP precedence across all three SDKs. `twin-credits-v0.1.json` fixes credits after wrapper/span merging in both report orders, including unknown usage and zero or unavailable credits. Node and Python run those twin cases; Go also merges `rudderotel` product-event spans with their wrapper twins, but does not run this fixture.

- `buffer_call` (Since v0.4): takes the same fields as `record_call`, but registers adapter finalization to report the call at the next pause or end. Used to check JSON snapshot handoff of buffered usage.

- Pause review operations (Since v0.4): `buffer_call.reenter_end` makes its adapter finalizer reenter `end(error)`; `bind_paused` consumes a bound stream that pauses and yields an approval (Node.js/Python only); `pause_on_shutdown_selection` arranges a pause after shutdown selection but before finalization, exercising the stale selection guard.

`pause-pending-usage-v0.1.json` also has `cross_sdk`, run by all three SDKs: `snapshots` (`written_by`, `snapshot`: the same two pending calls as each SDK writes them, plus the Python and Go encodings from before SDK-6111 and explicit `timestamp-epoch-ms` / `timestamp-rfc3339` entries that differ only in timestamps), `reports` (`source`: `"wrapper"` or `"span"`, `provider`, `model`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `started_ms`, `ended_ms`) and `expected` (`response`: a subset of the final `ai_response_received`; `call_events`: a subset of each `ai_llm_response_received`, in order). Restore each snapshot with `emitLlmCalls` on, record the reports and end; each SDK also checks that it still writes its own entry's `pending_calls`, `primary` and `outcome_hint`. Node/Python entries write epoch-ms timestamps; Go writes RFC3339Nano UTC text. All drivers restore both encodings and assert the same timing, ordering and counts. Current entries use the canonical selection objects; legacy entries use Python's positional lists. Restore and merge in both report orders; primary model/provider and the outcome must match `expected.response`.

## Audit normalization fixture

`audit-normalisation-v0.1.json` supplements conformance scenarios with direct helper inputs and wrapper/span reports that the scenario operations cannot express. It has `fixture_version: 1`, `spec_version: "0.4.0"` and arrays of cases, each with `input` and `expected`:

- `property_names`: input is an original custom key; expected gives `normalized`, `content` (dropped when capture is off) and `reserved` (cannot spoof an emitted SDK field even with capture on). Test content warnings twice and require one warning naming the original key. Set `agent_version: "v1"` for optional-field checks; `scope: "tool"` checks a declared search tool with a known result size. Unrelated custom names retain their spelling in emitted properties.
- `canonical_models`: input is a raw model ID; expected is the canonical ID. Assert helper, primary override, per-call model and breakdown model. A raw-ID price of input/output 2/4 per million with 1000/500 tokens yields USD 0.004; a raw-ID credit hook returns 7. Normalization must not change inputs to pricing or hooks.
- `calls`: input has `provider`, ordered `reports` (optional model/response ID/report-specific provider, wrapper/span source, tokens and optional epoch-millisecond window), optional raw-ID `prices` and `credits`. Record in order with no response IDs. Expected gives primary model, counts, totals and ordered model/call-count `groups`. Router providers resolve before grouping. Opposite sources and overlapping windows deduplicate equivalent canonical IDs; separate calls group without deduplicating, and distinct families/aliases never match.
  Adapter-specific cases carry `adapter: "claude-agent-sdk"` and are Node.js/Python only; Go must skip them because it has no Claude Agent SDK adapter. Their input replaces `reports` with raw SDK `messages` and a `resumed` flag. Consume every message through the Claude Agent SDK adapter without a baseline, within one interaction. With `standalone: true`, pass only the last message (the `result`) to `recordClaudeResult` / `record_claude_result` for that interaction instead, with no message stream and no primary model. Apply the same raw-ID `prices` and `credits`, and assert the same expected fields. Each raw usage row contributes its own call count; resumed usage is priced and credited per deployed ID before emitted rows group canonically. The credit hook must receive each raw ID once and return its configured credits multiplied by the reported call count.
- `statuses`: input is an ordered list of `call`, `hint`, `note` and `end` operations; call fields are `error_type`/`finish_reason`, markers are `status`/`error_type`. `hint` and `note` map to outcome hints, and `end` supplies explicit final options. Otherwise end normally after the steps. Expected is the exact response status and optional error type (absence matters). A later call invalidates earlier outcome hints, preserving existing marker-before-call behavior; explicit end options apply at finalization. Generic app errors preserve the latest provider/finish classification, while newer success or specific hints replace older ones and explicit non-generic app outcomes win.


`claude_turn_edges` covers Node/Python Claude adapter ordering and model memory across results. Each entry has `name`, `input.messages` (the same raw SDK message encoding as the adapter `calls` cases), `input.reverse_range` (start inclusive, end exclusive: reverse these messages for the other arrival order), and `expected.credit_calls` / `reverse_credit_calls` (ordered `[raw_model, agent_name_or_null, input_tokens]` tuples) plus `expected.response` (a subset of the final response). Configure a hook returning 1 and call events, start from an in-process resume or a JSON-restored empty pause snapshot, and consume the whole stream with an explicit empty usage baseline (`modelUsage` / `model_usage`: `{}`, `total_cost_usd`: 0). This isolates group ordering from inferred prior usage. Assert hook order, emitted call-token order and response fields in both arrival orders. Go has no Claude adapter and does not run these cases.

## emit-spans-v0.1.json

Language-neutral inputs for wrapper and manual spans; `fixture_version: 1`, span schema `0.1`, product spec `0.4.0`. Each `scenarios` entry contains `config` (`emit_spans`, `emit_llm_calls`, `capture_content`, default false), `clock.start_ms` (epoch milliseconds), `ids.trace_ids` (nonzero lowercase 32-hex IDs) and `ids.span_ids` (nonzero lowercase 16-hex IDs). Drivers consume trace IDs only for a new SDK trace and span IDs in request/manual entry order. Each interaction uses fixed identity `u`, interaction ID `fixture-interaction`, conversation ID `fixture-conversation`.

`steps` are recursive: `kind: "chat"` uses the provider (`openai`, `anthropic`, `aws.bedrock`, `gcp.gemini`) and model `m`, with input `hello`, output `answer` and 2 input / 1 output tokens. `kind: "span"` uses `name`, `operation` and optional `attributes` and child `steps`. Each step advances the clock by `advance_ms` after its children (or during a wrapper's provider response), then settles. `error` makes it throw that error unchanged. `attempt_durations_ms` replaces `advance_ms`: internal SDK attempts are simulated inside one provider request, advancing the clock by their sum. `afc_turns` adds that many Google automatic function-call/result pairs before the final response; they share one span and final product report.

`expected_spans` is in emission order. Match the listed properties and decoded OTLP attributes, permitting additional standard metadata. `expected_call_span_ids` is in product-call event order: an ID joins the span; null means the field must be omitted. Both spans and product events must validate against their unchanged JSON schemas.

Portable container descriptors use `$container`: `bytes` with byte `values`; `map` with `[key, value]` `entries`; `set` with `values`; `class` with `fields`; `bigint` with decimal string `value`; `symbol` for a nonportable key; and `cycle` with `value` and `self_key` (add a reference to that value itself). Drivers materialize the runtime containers before capture. These descriptors never appear on the wire. Strip native byte buffers/views, the serialized byte-buffer shape `{ "type": "Buffer", "data": [byte, ...] }` and cyclic edges; keep ordinary leaves and numeric-keyed objects, including numeric-valued Maps. Unsupported function, symbol and undefined array entries become null placeholders; cyclic array edges are omitted. Stringify string/number/boolean/bigint Map keys with `String()` (booleans lowercase), drop object/symbol keys, and turn Maps into objects and Sets into arrays. The `portable-containers` case must decode to `{ "1": "[email]", "2": "two", "true": ["keep"], "cycle": { "text": "keep" }, "class": { "text": "[email]" }, "numeric": { "1": 7, "2": 8 } }`.

Conformance scenarios with `config.emit_spans` normalize span IDs to `$span1`, `$span2`, etc., in emission order, using the same symbols on joined call events; trace IDs normalize to `$trace1`, etc. Span summaries retain source, GenAI attributes, parent IDs and status; times normalize to `<number>`. Pause snapshots optionally carry internal `sdk_trace_id` and pending-call `span_id`. Restoring pending events never replays a span.

## integration-spans-v0.1.json

Language-neutral framework lifecycle observations, with `fixture_version: 1`, span
schema `0.1` and product event spec `0.4.0`. Each scenario names its `integration`,
ordered `steps`, `execution` metadata and `expected_spans` in emission order. Run
IDs are symbolic driver inputs; drivers map them to their emitted W3C span IDs.
`start` has `run_id`, `operation`, `name` and optional `parent_run_id`; `end` has
`run_id` and optional `error`; `token` is a streaming observation. A returned tool
failure uses `tool_status_error: true`. Expected spans may specify `status_code`.
Vercel starts optionally list `tool_calls` / `tool_results` with symbolic tool `id`
and `name`, translated to response parts and the later step prompt. Operation names
are `invoke_agent`, `chat`, `execute_tool`, `retrieval`. Drivers translate these
observations into their native framework callbacks or messages. The fixture never
requires JavaScript classes, SDK-specific ID syntax or promise objects.

All scenarios run with spans on and content off/on. Expect each listed operation,
parent link, `rudderstack.span_source: integration` and valid span wire events;
content off must omit the driver's sentinel `private`. Roots without a parent use
null `parent_run_id`. An enclosing SDK span may be added by a driver-specific test.
Parallel starts precede either end; streaming uses the same start/end lifecycle
with optional token observations. Claude translates agent starts to Task/Agent
blocks and descendant parents to `parent_tool_use_id`; repeated assistant message
IDs share a model span. Agents handoff names select handoff spans. Vercel steps
have no expected tool execution spans: middleware cannot observe local executions.

`execution.mode` currently uses `async`; ports may add `thread_pool` or `goroutine`
and `worker_id` on steps without changing span/parent expectations. A port skips
integrations unavailable in that language: Vercel is Node-only, Python supports
the other three, and Go has no framework integrations. Future scenarios may add
`wrapper_call` observations to assert context deduplication and `error` endings.

Node's recorded `test/fixtures/integration-spans-off-main.json` compares product
JSON bytes at every callback checkpoint, before interaction end and before/after
flush, against the recorded `origin/main` commit. Regenerate intentionally with
`node scripts/generate-integration-spans-off-fixture.mjs <git-ref>`. The recorder
uses a Git archive, not a worktree, and installed pinned dependencies. IDs and the
clock are fixed driver inputs; `wrapperLibrary.version` becomes `<sdk-version>` so
release changes do not invalidate recorded bytes. No span await is added when
spans are off; the LangChain synchronous tracer protocol is disabled in that case.

## span-dedup-v0.1.json

One `ai_otel_span` per model call when SDK spans (`emitSpans`) and the RudderStack span processor both see it, with `fixture_version: 2`, span schema `0.1` and product event spec `0.4.0`. Each scenario has `emit_spans`, optional `processor: "simple" | "batch"` (default `simple`), an optional `requires: "integration"` (drivers without framework integrations skip it), a `tree` of nested scopes, `expected_spans`, `call_span` and `other_processors_see`. Run every scenario with `emitLlmCalls` on, the processor and a second plain processor on one provider, and a context manager that makes started spans active.

Tree nodes have a `kind`, a `label` and optional `children`, run in order inside the node's scope:

- `interaction`: an interaction whose `userId` is the label;
- `wrapper`: one provider wrapper call for model `label`; children run inside the provider request, as an instrumentation would;
